tax.text: He says he would lower taxes for working families, small businesses and agricultural producers, while also closing tax loopholes.
tax.quote: I will work to lower taxes for working families, small businesses, and ag producers.

wages.text: He introduced an Idaho bill to revise the minimum wage and says he supports policies that raise wages.
wages.quote: I support policies that raise wages, reward work and help more Americans support themselves without government assistance or subsidies.

housing.text: He supports increasing housing supply, including by rewarding cities for building more homes and loosening some rules on manufactured housing.
housing.quote: I will work to increase housing supply by promoting legislation that rewards cities for building more housing

schools.text: He says he will protect federal education funding for public schools, including Title I and rural schools.
schools.quote: I will protect federal education funding that supports Idaho students and ensures Title I and rural schools receive the resources they need.

immigration.text: He supports funding border enforcement while also pursuing legal immigration reforms and pathways for workers and others.
immigration.quote: we can secure our border while improving our legal immigration system.

guns.text: He says he would oppose new federal firearm bans and a federal gun-owner registry.
guns.quote: I will vote against new federal bans on firearms or magazines, a federal registry of gun owners

abortion.text: He supports Idaho’s Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act ballot initiative and says he would follow its outcome.
abortion.quote: I support Idaho’s Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act ballot initiative.

gender.text: As a state representative, he voted against a bill barring government entities from requiring employees and students to use preferred titles or pronouns.
gender.quote: CIVIL RIGHTS – Adds to existing law to prohibit governmental entities in the State of Idaho from compelling employees and students to use certain titles and pronouns.

health.text: He supports increasing competition and strengthening Idaho’s health-insurance marketplace while protecting coverage tax credits.
health.quote: I will also work across party lines to increase competition, improve affordability, and strengthen Idaho's health insurance marketplace.

wages.text: She said the federal government does not need to raise the minimum wage and that employers should decide whether higher pay improves competitiveness.
wages.quote: I don't believe the Federal government needs to raise the minimum wage.

sentencing.text: She supports rehabilitation instead of punitive incarceration for most drug offenses and opposes jailing people for minor marijuana possession.
sentencing.quote: I do support rehabilitation over punitive incarceration for most drug offenses.

immigration.text: She supports a faster, fully staffed legal immigration process and integration after vetting.
immigration.quote: Once someone has been vetted and cleared, they should be able to work, pay taxes, own property, and contribute fully — without years of additional waiting.

guns.text: In a candidate questionnaire, she said gun restrictions should be limited to people convicted of violent felonies and opposed red flag laws.
guns.quote: Restrictions on those convicted of violent felonies. No red flag laws. I don't care if you have a tank in your back yard, so long as you don't shoot my windows out.

abortion.text: She supports Idaho Proposition 1 and says the current law does not adequately allow medically necessary abortions.
abortion.quote: My faith recognizes the compassionate medical necessity of abortion in cases of rape, incest, serious threats to a mother’s life or health, and pregnancies where the fetus cannot survive beyond birth. Idaho’s current law falls short of even that standard.

tax.text: He says he would cut federal budgets across the board and abolish the estate tax.
tax.quote: I will fight to abolish the Death Tax that discourages parents from building wealth to pass on to their descendants.

wages.text: He says he would push to repeal minimum wage laws.
wages.quote: I can push to repeal the many laws and regulations that make it so difficult to run a legitimate business hiring American workers, including minimum wage laws

schools.text: He wants to dismantle government education and says parents should take responsibility for their children’s education.
schools.quote: As your Congressman, I will do everything in my power to dismantle the Education Industrial Complex.

immigration.text: He proposes closing the border to immigrants without a U.S. citizen landowner’s invitation and deporting them.
immigration.quote: Any uninvited immigrant should be deported to the country they most recently called home.

abortion.text: He describes abortion as homicide and says related laws belong at the state or local level.
abortion.quote: Since abortion is an act of homicide, any laws related to it belong at the state or local level.

cannabis.text: He supports ending the drug war and descheduling all substances, which would include cannabis.
cannabis.quote: I will push to de-schedule all substances from the Controlled Substances Schedules

tax.text: He supported making the 2017 Trump tax cuts permanent and described the bill as providing a historic tax cut.
tax.quote: provides working Americans with the largest tax cut in history

wages.text: He sponsored legislation defending workers’ ability to choose whether to join a union and voted against a procedural motion related to federal minimum-wage increases.
wages.quote: If that is not a union, that worker should not be forced to unionize.

schools.text: He voted against an amendment that would have eliminated education scholarships usable at public, private, or religious schools.
schools.quote: Statement of Purpose: To eliminate a program of qualified elementary and secondary education scholarships for public, private, or religious schools.

safety.text: Risch says he supports police funding and opposes defunding police.
safety.quote: As your Senator, I fight to defend—not defund—the police.

sentencing.text: Risch voted against the First Step Act of 2018.
sentencing.quote: Measure Number: S. 756 (First Step Act of 2018 )

guns.text: He voted against a gun-control bill, saying its provisions would erode Second Amendment rights.
guns.quote: infringing on Americans’ constitutional rights is not the answer to the challenges before us.

abortion.text: He said Roe v. Wade was wrongly decided and that he would protect the unborn.
abortion.quote: The most basic right we as humans have is the right to life.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He introduced legislation to define sex for Title IX purposes by reproductive biology and genetics at birth and to bar males from women’s sports.
gender.quote: Ensures Title IX provisions treat gender as “recognized based solely on a person’s reproductive biology and genetics at birth.”

cannabis.text: He joined colleagues in asking the president to keep marijuana classified as a Schedule I drug rather than reschedule it.
cannabis.quote: asking that marijuana remain a Schedule I drug.

energy.text: He supports expanding domestic oil drilling and other baseload power sources, and says energy policy should provide affordable energy.
energy.quote: I also support expanded drilling for domestic oil and the development of other sources of baseload power, such as geothermal, biomass, natural gas, and clean coal.

voting.text: Risch is an original SAVE Act cosponsor and says voters should show identification when registering and voting.
voting.quote: I am an original cosponsor of the SAVE Act and will continue working to make it law. We already have to show identification for many daily tasks, registering to vote and casting a ballot should be no different.
